name: Igun Street bronze casters (Igun Eronmwon), Benin City
subtitle: Igun Street in Benin City, Edo state, is a street of bronze casters who belong to a casters' guild said to have been sanctioned by Oba Oguola.

facts.label: Where
facts.value: Igun Street is a few kilometres off Ringroad Square in Benin City, Edo state, Nigeria.

facts.label: Date
facts.value: The craft's story, as told in this report, begins with a skilled artisan arriving in Benin City in about 1280 CE.

facts.label: Who runs it
facts.value: Casting is managed by the casters' guild, the same guild sanctioned by Oba Oguola centuries ago, according to caster Agbonmwenre.

facts.label: Who
facts.value: One caster says there are more than 20 casters on the street, each with a shed, all belonging to the Igun Bronze Casters Guild.

facts.label: How made
facts.value: In lost-wax casting, clay is applied over the wax model, heated so the wax melts out, and molten metal is poured into the mould.

facts.label: Change
facts.value: Casters say they first worked for the Oba's palace but now also sell to other buyers.

facts.label: Secrecy
facts.value: The guild has kept bronze casting limited to a few families.

parts.text: Igun Street in Benin City, Edo state, is a street of bronze casters who belong to a casters' guild said to have been sanctioned by Oba Oguola.
